title: What to Watch This Week: Netflix Drops a Triple Bomb, SonyLIV Brings the Grit, and Dhamaal Returns to Theatres
excerpt: From a courtroom reunion thirty years in the making to a three-hour Telugu epic and a Tamil murder mystery, this week’s streaming lineup is absurdly stacked. Here are our picks.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Netflix releases three major Indian films on July 10, enhancing weekend viewing options.
  • Ikka features a long-awaited reunion of Sunny Deol and Akshaye Khanna after 30 years.
  • Peddi is a three-hour Telugu sports drama showcasing a remarkable transformation story.
  • Balti is a gritty Malayalam kabaddi drama highlighting personal rivalries and brotherhood.
  • Dhamaal 4 opens in theaters with strong early reviews, promising family-friendly entertainment.
Streaming Highlights This Week
›Ikka: Sunny Deol and Akshaye Khanna reunite after 30 years.
›Peddi: A three-hour Telugu epic about a wrestler's journey.
›Balti: A Malayalam kabaddi drama focusing on rivalry and brotherhood.
›Dhamaal 4: Early reviews score 3.5-4/5, promising family fun.

Netflix just dropped a bomb on your weekend plans. Three major Indian films hit the platform on the same day — and the global lineup is stacked too. Whether you're in the mood for a courtroom showdown, a Telugu sports epic, or a comedy that'll make your aunties text the family group chat, this week has something. Here's what's worth your time.

Ikka — Netflix, July 10

The headline reunion: Sunny Deol and Akshaye Khanna, together on screen for the first time since *Border* in 1997. Nearly thirty years later, they're no longer fighting on the same side. Deol plays a celebrated defence lawyer who's blackmailed into defending Khanna's character — a man he knows is guilty. The courtroom sequences are tense, the moral dilemma is real, and the pairing alone makes this compulsory viewing. Tillotama Shome and Dia Mirza add depth to what could've been a one-note thriller. Directed by Siddharth P. Malhotra. If you watch one thing this week, make it this.

Where to watch in the US/UK/Canada: Netflix, globally.

Pati Patni Aur Woh Do — Netflix, July 10

Ayushmann Khurrana as a Benaras forest officer who tells one small lie and watches his life implode. Sara Ali Khan, Rakul Preet Singh, and Wamiqa Gabbi orbit around his escalating panic in a comedy of errors that's exactly what it sounds like — chaotic, loud, and family-friendly. It's not going to win awards, but it's the perfect film for a group watch where nobody can agree on what to stream. Director Mudassar Aziz knows this formula, and the supporting cast — Vijay Raaz, Tigmanshu Dhulia — is stacked with scene-stealers.

![Sunny Deol — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/d9/Sunny_Paaji_2024.jpg)

> "Early reviews call it a "complete family entertainer" (3.5–4/5 from first screenings)."

Where to watch: Netflix, globally.

Peddi — Netflix, July 9

Ram Charan in a rural sports-action drama that runs over three hours and somehow justifies every minute. He plays a sugarcane labourer who transforms into a wrestler, loses his leg, and comes back as a blade-running para-athlete. It's sweeping, emotional, and exactly the kind of epic Telugu cinema that plays differently when you're watching on your couch in New Jersey versus a packed single-screen in Andhra Pradesh. Janhvi Kapoor co-stars. Available in Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, and Malayalam with subtitles. Not for the faint of heart — or those short on time.

Where to watch: Netflix, globally.

Balti — SonyLIV, July 10

Here's the dark horse. Shane Nigam's 25th film is a Malayalam kabaddi drama set in a border town where the sport is everything. Four champion players dominate the streets, their brotherhood is tight — until personal rivalries turn dangerous. It's gritty, physical, and exactly the kind of South Indian cinema that the diaspora has been gravitating toward post-RRR. Available in Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Hindi. If you've been sleeping on SonyLIV, this is your wake-up call.

Where to watch: SonyLIV (available in India and select international markets).

Parimala and Co — ZEE5, July 10

A Tamil black comedy about a middle-class Chennai family whose lives implode when a goon harassing their daughter turns up dead — and they're the prime suspects. Starring Jayaram, Urvashi, and Mysskin (yes, the director, acting), with Yogi Babu providing comic relief. Director Pandiraaj builds paranoia inside a single household as family members start suspecting each other. Sharp, funny, and deeply Tamil in its sensibility. Think *Drishyam* meets *Kaithi*, but funnier.

Where to watch: ZEE5 (available globally).

![Akshaye Khanna — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/7f/Akshaye_Khanna_at_the_launch_of_GUJCON_CRF_and_PRF.jpg)

Hamnet — Netflix, July 6

For something entirely different: Jessie Buckley and Paul Mescal in a period drama about William Shakespeare and Anne Hathaway (the original one) navigating the loss of their young son. It's quiet, devastating, and beautifully acted. Not Bollywood, not action, not comedy. Just two extraordinary performers in a story about grief, love, and what gets created when everything else falls apart. Already drawing comparisons to *The Lost Daughter*. It's been on Netflix since July 6 — catch up if you missed it.

Where to watch: Netflix, globally.

The Westies — Prime Video, July 12

Closing the week: J.K. Simmons, David Harbour, and Jeremy Strong in a gritty 1980s Hell's Kitchen crime drama about Irish-American gangsters warring with the Italian Mafia over construction rackets. Directed by Allen Hughes (*Menace II Society*). This one's for the prestige-TV crowd who miss the energy of early *Boardwalk Empire*. Arrives Sunday — perfect for a solo binge.

Where to watch: Amazon Prime Video, globally.

Bonus: Dhamaal 4 — Theatres, July 10

If you're in India or near a theatre running it: Ajay Devgn, Arshad Warsi, Riteish Deshmukh, and Jaaved Jaaferi are back for another round of slapstick treasure-hunt madness. Early reviews call it a "complete family entertainer" (3.5–4/5 from first screenings). It's the kind of film that works best in a packed theatre with strangers laughing around you. The franchise reportedly teases a fifth instalment in the end credits. Box office is tracking at ₹12-14 crore for opening day.

---

*That's seven streaming picks and one theatrical event. Your weekend is planned. You're welcome.*
